In SCOP 1.75, PDB 1acc chain A (anthrax protective antigen, 735 residues) was a single whole-chain domain, d1acca_ (sunid 43828, f.11.1.1, 'anthrax protective antigen'). The description '1acc A:' has no residue range, so the whole chain was one unit. In the current release, 2.08, the same chain is split into two domains: d1acca2 (1acc A:14-225, sunid 238522, b.179.1.1, PA14, fold b.179 'Anthrax protective antigen N-terminal-like', class b all-beta) and d1acca1 (1acc A:226-735, sunid 238521, f.60.1.1, 'Anthrax protective antigen C-terminal-like', fold f.60, class f membrane and cell surface). Residues 1-13 are not assigned to either 2.08 domain. The 1.75 SID d1acca_ is absent from 2.08, and the 2.08 SIDs do not resolve in 1.75; cross-release work has to go through the release-specific records, not the SID strings.

What this reveals: the 1.75 whole-chain assignment treated two structurally distinct modules as one domain. The later split puts them in different classes (all-beta vs membrane/cell-surface), so they share no fold, superfamily or family in SCOPe. A SCOPe domain is a classification unit chosen by curators from the structure, and its boundaries and fold assignments can be revised as evidence changes. The split therefore does not show that the old 'domain' was a single evolutionary module. It shows that the classification unit was wrong, and that the two parts have separate histories: PA14-like N-terminal and C-terminal folds. The 2.08 sequence cluster representative 3tewA is 96.9% identical over 735 residues. That is sequence similarity to a cluster representative, not structural evidence, and I did not check any structural hits.

Homology-search implications: do not use the 1.75 f.11.1.1 label as a whole-chain template or as a homology transfer for this chain. Search the 14-225 and 226-735 segments separately, and use 2.08 labels when the target is a current release. Transferring a 1.75 hit to a 2.08 domain, or treating the two 2.08 domains as one homology unit, would be unsafe because they differ at the class and fold level. Each domain's classification applies only to that domain, not to other proteins or to other structures with the same whole-chain label.
